Migration report

Check whether an appliance's whole configuration survives a move to a target firmware build — what blocks, what is renamed, what changes behind your back — before the upgrade window.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsbackups.create backups.restore
📍 WhereAutomation → Migration Report (URL /web/migration-report/); appliance page → Migration Report; Upgrade Flow stage 1

What is it?#

The Migration report checks every object and field an appliance holds today against what SATOM knows about a target firmware build, and gives one verdict: ready, ready with warnings, blocked, or cannot assess. It answers the question every upgrade window starts with — what of this box's configuration does the new build reject, rename or change? — before the image is uploaded.

What does it do?#

  • Reads the appliance's newest show full-configuration backup (or one you choose) in memory and compares it with the target build's CLI schema in the API library.
  • Classifies each finding:
Class Examples
block an object or field the box uses is gone in the target; an enum value the target no longer accepts; a value out of range; a type the value does not fit
translate a rename covered by an operator rename map
warn a probable rename (same CLI attribute id, not mapped yet); a default that changed under a field left at its default; no evidence for the object on the target; a target not completely measured (with the percentage)
info new objects and fields in the target (with defaults when known); removed fields the box does not use
  • Never stores the report and never puts a configuration value in it — only names, counts of affected rows and facts about the build.
  • Says where its build knowledge comes from: Knowledge from <pack> (<date>), with a stale badge when the newest knowledge pack is older than 30 days (3.0). Rename candidates a pack proposes are never applied — only an operator rename map translates.

Requirements#

  • At least one configuration backup of the appliance in the vault (a show full-configuration dump). Without one the verdict is cannot assess.
  • The target build has a CLI schema in the library — harvested (Schema builds) or imported from a knowledge pack.
  • A FortiWeb, FortiADC or FortiGate appliance. (A FortiGate has no stored configuration backup yet, so it reads cannot assess.)

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open the page, read and export reports backups.create or backups.restore (the Upgrade Flow's gate)

An appliance of another ADOM, or hidden by maintenance, answers 404.

How to use#

Check one appliance#

  1. Open Automation → Migration Report (or Migration Report on the appliance page).
  2. Pick the Appliance and a Target build. The list offers only builds whose CLI schema SATOM has.
  3. Click Check.
  4. Read the verdict and its reason, the Configuration dump it used, Target build measured (how complete the target is), the Per object counts and every finding.
  5. Export with JSON or CSV for the change record.

Confirm a rename#

  1. A rename_candidate warning names the old and new field.
  2. If it is a real rename, record it on API field renames (API library).
  3. Run the report again: the row is now translate.

Read it in the Upgrade Flow#

In stage 1 of the Upgrade Flow, each appliance shows the migration verdict for the move its newest pre-upgrade recorded, with a link to the full report. At most 20 appliances are assessed per page render; the rest link to their report.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Appliance the box to check Yes fweb-01
Target build exact firmware build Yes 8.0.6
Backup a specific vault backup instead of the newest No backup 1207

Example#

🧪Example — FortiWeb 7.6.8 → 8.0.6

A FortiWeb 7.6.8 with a production-sized configuration: 212 objects checked, 10 block / 0 translate / 11 warn / 104 info, verdict blocked. Blocks: mobile-app-identification holds a value 8.0.6 no longer accepts; waf/file-exception-policy and the file-exception-policy field are gone; system/ntp syncsamples is gone. Warnings: probable renames token-header → jwt-token-name, appsec-cloud-connection-url → threat-analytics-authurl, sql-xss-sbd-op → sbd-op; a type change on an exception-element ip; the target is not completely measured.

Result#

  • A verdict and a list of findings on screen; nothing is written anywhere.
  • JSON or CSV downloads with names and counts only.

Troubleshooting#

Verdict "cannot assess"#

Possible causes - No usable show full-configuration dump in the vault. - The source build is unknown (no firmware recorded on the dump or the appliance). - The target build has no CLI schema in the library.

Solution 1. Take a backup of the appliance; run a firmware check; or harvest/import the target build.

Verification - The report shows a verdict other than cannot assess.

"No build of this product has a CLI schema in the API library yet: import an API pack or harvest a box on the target build."#

Possible causes - The library has no tree schema for any build of that product.

Solution 1. Import the newest knowledge pack (Knowledge packs), or harvest an appliance from Schema builds.

"No appliance of a supported product is visible here."#

Possible causes - The ADOM holds no FortiWeb, FortiADC or FortiGate appliance you can see.

A warning says the target is only partly measured#

Possible causes - Some target fields have an unknown channel (empty tables were never read).

Solution 1. Read the percentage; what is not measured cannot be guaranteed. A knowledge pack with lab rows raises it.

Advanced#

Advanced Console

sudo satom execute migration report <appliance> --target <build> [--backup <id>] prints the move, the verdict, the counts and the first ten block and warn rows; the global --json flag prints the full report. It runs flask apilib migration-report as the service account. See CLI.

Advanced What the report reads, and its limits

The dump tells what the device uses; the target's tree tells what the build has. show full-configuration prints only fields that apply under each row's current settings, so a field absent from a dump is not absent on the build. A target older than the source runs the same checks, labelled downgrade. The report proves a value is accepted, not that a feature behaves the same — read the vendor upgrade notes too (Release notes).

#migration report#upgrade#downgrade#target build#firmware#verdict#blocked#rename#default changed#show full-configuration#export#csv#json
